values.name: Sodium (Na+)
values.notes: Regulates fluid volume, blood pressure, neuromuscular function.

values.name: Potassium (K+)
values.notes: Critical for cardiac conduction, neuromuscular excitability. High risk for dysrhythmias.

values.name: Calcium (Ca2+)
values.notes: Bone health, muscle contractions, clotting. Watch for Chvostek's and Trousseau's signs.

values.name: Magnesium (Mg2+)
values.notes: Enzyme activation, neuromuscular transmission, cardiac membrane stability.

values.name: Chloride (Cl-)
values.notes: Maintains osmotic pressure and acid-base balance.

values.name: Phosphorus (PO4 3-)
values.notes: Inverse relationship with calcium.

values.name: White Blood Cells (WBC)
values.notes: Infection/inflammation marker. Neutropenic precautions if < 1,000.

values.name: Red Blood Cells (RBC)
values.notes: Oxygen carrying capacity.

values.name: Hemoglobin (Hgb)
values.notes: Transfusion often indicated when < 7-8 g/dL.

values.name: Hematocrit (Hct)
values.notes: Roughly 3x Hemoglobin. Elevated with hemoconcentration/dehydration.

values.name: Platelets
values.notes: Bleeding precautions when < 50,000. Risk of spontaneous bleed when < 20,000.

values.name: Prothrombin Time (PT)
values.notes: Evaluates extrinsic pathway. Monitored in Warfarin therapy.

values.name: International Normalized Ratio (INR)
values.notes: Mechanical heart valves target: 2.5 - 3.5. Antidote: Vitamin K.

values.name: Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (aPTT)
values.notes: Therapeutic Heparin is 1.5 - 2.5x normal. Antidote: Protamine sulfate.

values.name: D-Dimer
values.notes: Used to rule out DVT and Pulmonary Embolism.

values.name: pH
values.notes: < 7.35 = Acidosis | > 7.45 = Alkalosis

values.name: PaCO2 (Respiratory Component)
values.notes: > 45 = Acidosis (hypoventilation) | < 35 = Alkalosis (hyperventilation)

values.name: HCO3 (Metabolic Component)
values.notes: < 22 = Acidosis (renal/DKA) | > 26 = Alkalosis (vomiting/suctioning)

values.name: PaO2
values.notes: Hypoxemia when < 80 mmHg on room air.

values.name: SaO2
values.notes: Target > 92% in general, 88-92% in chronic COPD.

values.name: Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN)
values.notes: Elevated in renal failure, dehydration, high protein intake, GI bleeding.

values.name: Serum Creatinine
values.notes: Most specific indicator of kidney function.

values.name: Fasting Blood Glucose
values.notes: Hypoglycemia (< 70) requires rapid simple carbohydrates (15-15 rule).

values.name: Glycosylated Hemoglobin (HbA1c)
values.notes: Reflects average glucose over past 2-3 months.

values.name: Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR)
values.notes: Stages chronic kidney disease. < 15 indicates kidney failure (ESRD).

values.name: Total Bilirubin
values.notes: Jaundice typically visible when > 2.5 - 3.0 mg/dL.

values.name: Serum Albumin
values.notes: Maintains oncotic pressure. Low in malnutrition, cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome.

values.name: Ammonia
values.notes: Elevated in hepatic encephalopathy. Treated with Lactulose.

values.name: ALT (Alanine Aminotransferase)
values.notes: Liver-specific injury marker.

values.name: AST (Aspartate Aminotransferase)
values.notes: Elevated in liver disease and muscular damage.

values.name: Amylase & Lipase
values.notes: Lipase is more specific for acute pancreatitis.

values.name: Troponin I
values.notes: Gold standard for Acute Myocardial Infarction. Rises within 3-4 hours.

values.name: B-Type Natriuretic Peptide (BNP)
values.notes: Elevated in heart failure (> 400 indicates acute decompensation).

values.name: Total Cholesterol
values.notes: Cardiovascular risk factor.

values.name: LDL Cholesterol
values.notes: "Bad cholesterol".

values.name: HDL Cholesterol
values.notes: "Good cholesterol".

values.name: Triglycerides
values.notes: Elevated with poor glycemic control, high alcohol intake.

values.name: Digoxin (Lanoxin)
values.notes: Toxicity: halos, nausea, bradycardia. Hold if HR < 60 bpm. Antidote: Digibind.

values.name: Lithium
values.notes: Toxicity > 1.5: ataxia, coarse tremor, confusion. Maintain adequate salt/water intake.

values.name: Phenytoin (Dilantin)
values.notes: Toxicity: nystagmus, ataxia, slurred speech. Encourage good oral hygiene (hyperplasia).

values.name: Theophylline
values.notes: Toxicity: tachycardia, dysrhythmias, seizures, tremors.

values.name: Vancomycin (Trough)
values.notes: Drawn 30 min before next dose. Monitor BUN/creatinine (nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity).
